_notes: ONE DECK FOR THE WHOLE NIGHT (owner rule 2026-08-03). The vole fight
lays down `deck` -- 21 cards, ordered so the deck is drawn back-to-front:
Ferocity first, then Shadow, then Guile, then Moonlight. Nothing is ever
added again, so the spool only ever goes DOWN across the prologue. Each
fight names its `opening_cards` so the beat that teaches a humour deals
that humour, whatever the player spent before it.
Length target: about one mission -- four fights, and no story page that
Lines given as {text, rule:true} are the GAME talking, not Ash; the story
screen sets those in smallcaps accent so rules never read as narration.

lines: Dusk over Hollowmere. The lamps going up, one by one, like the city buttoning its coat.
She puts the kettle on when the lamps go up. I am punctual. She is predictable. The arrangement works.
Tonight calls for a gift. A vole, ideally. Voles say what flowers cannot.

scenes.art_desc: Ash pressed low on rooftop tiles, stalking an unaware vole near a chimney pot, warm dusk light
lines: There. Under the chimney pot. Fat, smug, unaware.
Tonight the world is simple, and the world is RED.

notes: ❋ FEROCITY, the red energy — the oldest there is, and the only one a cat is born knowing. It pays for POUNCE.

coach.text: The opposition. Tonight: one vole of tremendous conviction.
Its life is a red thread. Claws do the unstitching.
It telegraphs its next move here. Honesty is its one virtue.
The heart: your lives-worth of tonight. Guard it.
The shield: GUARD soaks a hit, then fades at turn's end.
The spool: energy still wound in your deck. It only ever unwinds — spent stays spent.
Paws are actions. Placing an energy anywhere spends one. Three a turn.
Your hand is ENERGY — tonight, all Ferocity.
Tap POUNCE.
Two empty pips, two Ferocity owed. Feed it one.
One to go. A skill fires only once every pip is filled.
Full. A willing card. Tap USE.
Four off its thread — that is what a powered card buys.
And two energies lighter. The spool does not rewind.
Two paws gone with them. Placing energy is the cost of doing anything.
A breath left in it. SCRATCH — free, once a turn. Finish politely.

lines: Acquired. Thoughtfully dead.
She will say 'not on the table', and mean 'thank you'.
The vole declines to be a gift tonight. Dignity intact. Mostly.
She will have to make do with my company, which is worth several voles.

scenes.art_desc: The Shambles at night: market stalls sleeping under canvas, crooked timber shopfronts, one lit lantern
lines: Below: the Shambles. Eight bells from the tower. There is no ninth bell — there used to be.
Between the chimneys: a thread of silver light, thin as a hair, humming. Not mine. Not hers.
I did not chase it. I am a professional.
Street level. The fog rolls up from the Mere, and the shadows deepen — deep enough to wear.
Something small and hungry climbs out of the gutter: a GUTTER-WISP.
Bottle-sized. It eats small lies, and it heard mine — the one about not chasing the silver thread. It has come back for seconds.

notes: ❋ SHADOW, the black energy. It hides and it wards — and in this fog it costs one less.

coach.text: Every fight opens with the going-in. STALK it — spend 2 Shadow to begin unseen.
Two Shadow went on the entrance. That is what an approach costs — up front, out of hand.
Every place has a rule. In this fog, Shadow costs one less — so SLINK is free here.
Read the chip up top. Some moves come for your HEALTH. Others come for your HAND — and a guard stops teeth, not fingers.
SLINK blocks 3. Free in the fog — but only three times tonight.
Nothing owed. Tap USE.
Three guard, until the turn ends. It will soak a bite. It will not stop a theft — energy already fed onto a card is the only energy nothing can take.
Note the count on POUNCE: two left. Charges do not come back until a long rest at the Mantel. Spend them like a cat, not like a dog.
When your paws are spent, END TURN. The night moves too.

lines: The wisp reconsidered its position on my honesty.
I let it keep its opinions. The night is too strange to argue with weather made of appetite.
Something is wrong tonight, and it is not the wisp. No pigeons. Pigeons are never quiet; quiet is against their religion.
The lamps on Needle Lane are lit wrong — and the Lamplighters never miss. The dog at Number Twelve is awake and does not bark, which it has never once failed to do.
Halfway down, the fog stops being fog.
It has sleeves. A collar. The shape of a person who is not in it — and every cut thread on this street is running towards it, like water finding a drain.
It turns what it has instead of a face towards me. Whatever unpicked the lamps is still working, and I am standing in its light.

notes: ❋ GUILE, the green patience — and MOONLIGHT, which is hers. Moonlight is WILD: one Moonlight card pays for anything you own.

coach.text: A RAG-WRAITH: clothes whose owner is missing. Not dead — missing. It is above your weight, and it knows it.
PURR heals 2 a turn for two turns — but breaks if you're hit. Purr behind a block.
You do not have to win this. SLIP AWAY — though it gets its move in as you go.

lines: Three streets before I stop, and I stop because my legs decide it, not me.
Nothing followed. Nothing is missing. Ash: one. The weather: nothing. I would like that entered in the record.
And yet: it was not hunting me. It was WORKING. Whatever it is doing to this street, I interrupted about as much as a fly interrupts a window.
It comes apart in the middle of the road, and the threads it was pulling go slack.
That was not supposed to be possible, and I do not feel clever about it. I feel like something let go.
Her window is ahead now. Dark. Her window is never dark.
Two ways home from here.
The long way passes the Lamplighters' hall — whatever silenced the lamps went wrong there first.
The fast way is over the fences. Now. While the kettle still screams.
choices: The long way — see what silenced the lamps

scenes.art_desc: Lamplighters' guild hall interior, abandoned mid-shift: racked ladders, cold kettle, one silver thread glinting on a lamp-hook
lines: The hall: door open, ladders racked, kettle cold. Nobody.
Caught on a lamp-hook: a thread of silver. HER stitching. She was here tonight. Why was she HERE?
notes: ❋ Her Stitching joins your deck — a Moonlight 2, and the only card of its kind you own.

lines: Out of the hall and eleven streets home, and I do not remember eight of them.
The fog thins near the Mere. Ordinary houses. Ordinary gates. A cat crossing an ordinary city at an unreasonable speed.
Her street. Her gate. Her drainpipe, the one I have used nine hundred times.

scenes.art_desc: Ash in full sprint leaping between fence tops at night, fog blurred with speed, a dark window ahead
lines: Over the fences, under the gate, up the drainpipe I have used nine hundred times.
Fast enough that something inside is still... busy.
In through the workroom window. A door has never once been an obstacle. It is, however, always an insult.
The house is doing the wrong thing with sound. A kettle screaming and nobody going to it.
The threads on the walls — cut. All of them. Hanging like torn hems.
Forty years of her work, and every single one snipped at the same height, as if by someone tidying.
The room is very cold and very quiet and I have not gone through to the parlor yet.

scenes.art_desc: The Unpicked: a person-shaped absence woven from the room's own unravelled threads, standing in a doorway
lines: Something is standing in the parlor doorway, wearing the room.
It is person-shaped the way a coat on a hook is person-shaped, and it is made of her threads — it has been pulling them out of the walls and putting them ON.
It is still working. It does not stop when it sees me. That is the part I will keep: it looked at me, decided I was not an interruption, and went back to it.
Every hair I have is standing up. Good. Let them.

coach.text: MOONLIGHT — the pale card. It is WILD: it pays any cost you own, whatever the colour of the pips. Hers always did work on anything.
And CONCENTRATE: give up the whole turn to stare one spent energy back onto the spool. It is the last thing you have when the hand is empty. It will not be enough. Do it anyway.

hints.1: Moonlight is hers, and it is WILD — a Moonlight card pays for anything you own. Spend it. Spend everything.
hints.5: Her room makes Moonlight cheaper. She is still helping. It still will not be enough.

lines: Something comes back on before I do. Hearing, I think.
Floorboards under one cheek. The smell of cold hearth. Four paws — count them. Four.
Whatever was standing in the doorway is not standing in the doorway. Get up, Ash.
The parlor.
Elspeth in her chair. The light gone out of her hands.
The kettle is still screaming. It has been screaming this whole time, and I did not hear it until now.
She hates it when it does that.
I took it off the fire. One paw. It took three tries. Nobody will ever know.
The thread at my chest — the one that was always hers — cut.
Not quite. One strand left. Thin as spite. Running out under the window, into the city.
Then that is where we are going.

_hollow_court_notes: Played as PAGES, not one block of text (owner 2026-08-04: the first
visit read as though Ash already knew the place). Page 1 is the room
before anyone speaks; page 2 is the Clerk, with a line Ash gets to pick;
page 3 says plainly what dying costs. Every death after the first uses
the short form, because by then he does know the place.
Schema: {lines, portrait?, choices?, answers?} — see game.gd _play_pages.

lines: The cold goes first. Then the noise. Then the part of me that was worried about the noise.
What is left over is standing in a corridor that is all filing and no building, under a ceiling too far up to be a ceiling.
Nothing hurts. I would like it on record that I find this deeply suspicious.

hollow_court_first.art_desc: The Hollow Court: a translucent clerk at a lamplit desk before endless filing shelves, one empty chair facing him
lines: A desk. A lamp. A queue of one, and the one is me.
The Clerk does not look up. 'Name?'
answers: 'Everyone here is something.' He turns a page without touching it. '...Vane's familiar. There you are.'
'Nine allotted. One spent. Try to be interesting about the rest.'
'Needle Lane.' Something moves behind the spectacles that is almost interest. 'Yes. We have had a busy evening from Needle Lane.'
'Vane's familiar. Nine allotted, one spent.' He does not say whose the busy evening was. I do not ask, because I already know.
The silence goes on long enough to become a position. He allows it, and then writes something anyway.
'Vane's familiar. Nine allotted, one spent.' — 'You will find that not answering is also an answer, and that I have a great deal of filing.'

lines: 'The arrangement, since it is your first: you are difficult to kill and not impossible. When you are killed you come here, we take the Toll, and you go back up.'

lines.text: Dying costs a life and a quarter of your banked gleam. Whatever was in your satchel stays where you dropped it. Nothing else is lost — not your kit, not your case, not what you have already worked out.

lines: 'The first visit is complimentary. Do consider it a courtesy rather than a habit.'
The stamp comes down. It is, I notice, a paw print. Neither of us remarks on this.
The stairs up are longer than the fall down. They always are.
The desk again. The lamp again. The Clerk does not look up.
'Back so soon. The form remembers you, which saves us both time.'
The Toll is taken. Professionally. Almost gently.
The stairs up are longer than the fall down. They always are.

_mantel_notes: Shown ONCE, the first time Ash comes home to a room he now lives in
alone (flag: mantel_taught). The room starts nearly bare on purpose --
QuestGate.doors() opens each door as it is earned -- so the tour is a
tour of what is there, not a preview of what is not.

mantel_coach.text: Her parlor. Cold, and still hers. This is where a night begins and, with luck, ends.
What the city is asking of you gets pinned to the chimney breast. One thing tonight. There will be more; there is always more.
Tap a note to take the work. A prowl is two or three rooms deep — press on for a bigger purse, or come home while you still can.
Gleam. Buttons, mostly, and the occasional tooth. It buys cards, and it is what the Court takes when you die.
Lives, the spool, and deeds recorded. The spool is the one to watch: it does not refill mid-prowl.
One door for now — the Casebook, which is only my own memory and has always been open. The rest of this room opens when I have earned it. Find the Magpie first.
And that. For when you want to go back and stand in the worst night again. I do not recommend it. I do it constantly.

unpicked_won: It comes apart. Thread by thread. That was not supposed to happen.
Somewhere below the city, a clerk files something under 'irregular'.
